_what_this_is: Sync state for the Notion -> GitHub mirror of the UEFN Field Notes.
Each entry records the Notion page a file was translated from, and that page's
last_edited_at as of the last sync. It exists so a future session with no memory
of earlier ones can tell genuine upstream drift from mere translation differences.
It is COMMITTED ON PURPOSE - do not add it to .gitignore. Ignored, it would live
only inside one ephemeral session container and help nobody after that session ends.
_how_to_sync: 1. Fetch the hub page and walk its whole subtree, including sub-pages of topic
pages - new material has twice arrived as a child page, not an edit.
2. For each page, compare its last_edited_at against notion_last_edited_at below.
Only the pages that moved need translating; leave the rest alone.
3. A page in the subtree with no entry here is unmirrored: it needs a new file.
4. Update every notion_last_edited_at you acted on, plus last_sync, in the same
commit as the content. A manifest that lags the content is worse than none.
Direction is one way: Notion -> GitHub. If a repo file carries something Notion
lacks, flag it for the humans to copy upstream - never overwrite it away.
_translation_policy: This repo is a public translation, not a copy. Epic and platform identifiers stay
names, log lines). Project-owned identifiers are genericised: project and asset
names, persona names, machine and account names, personal names, internal build
and experiment codes. Keep the findings, the dates, the evidence types and the
struck-through corrections exactly as they are - the epistemics ARE the content.
Sub-pages are mirrored with a letter suffix on the parent's number (02a, 06a).
_privacy_rule: This file is public. What may live here: file names, Notion page IDs and URLs,
page titles, and timestamps. Page IDs and URLs are addresses, not credentials -
the workspace is private and Notion still requires auth, so a leaked ID grants
nobody anything. The titles are already public in the README structure table.
What must NEVER be cached here: page content or excerpts, titles of private pages
outside the mirrored hub, tokens, API keys, or personal data. If a future sync
wants content-level diffing, keep that cache OUT of the repo - the moment this
file holds content, it stops being safe to publish.
